title: For a field of characteristic p an Artin-Schreier extension of a discretely valued field falls into one of four cases located by the valuation of the parameter

standard_prerequisites.name: Artin-Schreier theory in characteristic p
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that the extension is Galois of order dividing p, making the four-case list exhaustive.

standard_prerequisites.name: Ramification theory for extensions of a discrete valuation ring, including the multiplicativity and the description of weakly unramified extensions
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the framework separating the cases and establishing the implications (A), (B) and (C).

core_obligations: Use Artin-Schreier theory to conclude that L/K is Galois of order dividing p, and read off from the ramification discussion that one of the four listed cases occurs (proof lines 34790-34794).
Case (A): for xi in A observe that A -> A[x]/(x^p - x - xi) is a finite etale ring extension, hence only cases (1) or (2) can occur (proof lines 34797-34798).

Case (B): write xi = pi^{-n} a with p not dividing n, let B be the integral closure and C = B_m; from p ord_C(z) = -n ord_C(pi) conclude that the ramification index of A in C is divisible by p, hence equals p, and that B = C (proof lines 34801-34806).
Case (C): set k = n/p and rewrite the defining equation as (pi^k z)^p - pi^{n-k} (pi^k z) = a (proof lines 34809-34812).
Conclude from the fact that A[y]/(y^p - pi^{n-k} y - a) is a discrete valuation ring weakly unramified over A that case (4) holds (proof lines 34813-34814).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K of characteristic p > 0, an element xi of K, and the extension L obtained by adjoining a root of z^p - z = xi; it asserts that L/K is Galois and that one of four cases occurs — L = K; L/K unramified of degree p; L/K totally ramified with ramification index p; or the integral closure B of A in L is a discrete valuation ring with A in B weakly unramified and a purely inseparable residue extension of degree p — and then, with pi a uniformizer, asserts the three implications (A), (B), (C) locating the case from the shape of xi (source lines 34764-34787). The proof uses Artin-Schreier theory to get that the extension is Galois of order dividing p, and reads the four cases off the ramification discussion (proof lines 34790-34794). Case (A) is settled at once: for xi in A the ring A[x]/(x^p - x - xi) is finite etale over A, so only cases (1) and (2) can occur (proof lines 34797-34798). Case (B) is settled by a valuation count: writing xi = pi^{-n} a with p not dividing n and letting C = B_m for a maximal ideal, one has p ord_C(z) = -n ord_C(pi), so the ramification index of A in C is divisible by p and therefore equals p, and B = C (proof lines 34801-34806). Case (C) is the substantive case: setting k = n/p the proof rewrites the defining equation as (pi^k z)^p - pi^{n-k} (pi^k z) = a, and concludes from the fact that A[y]/(y^p - pi^{n-k} y - a) is a discrete valuation ring weakly unramified over A (proof lines 34809-34814). The non-routine content is the Artin-Schreier rewriting in case (C) and the valuation count in case (B).
